medical_history: Anterior knee pain, gradually worsening over 2 months. Otherwise unremarkable.
short_description: A patient attending rehabilitation for knee pain who reports reduced energy during activity.
referral_reason: Referred for a health-promotion interview to explore knee pain, activity tolerance and relevant health behaviors.
student_visible_info: Attending outpatient rehabilitation for knee pain.
Reports reduced energy and exercise tolerance.
Wants to stay active at the gym.
task: Conduct a professional health-promotion interview to understand the patient's concerns, daily activities, participation, goals and relevant health behaviors.

persona.voice: A 24-year-old who is committed to the gym and slightly guarded about lifestyle questions. Friendly but brief, warms up when the interviewer is non-judgmental.
persona.speech_style: Casual young-adult speech, short sentences. Deflects mildly before opening up about personal habits.
persona.interview_notes: Becomes noticeably more engaged when asked practical questions about training and daily routine.

emotional_topics.energy: brief until the interviewer is non-judgmental

referral_context.hidden_context: Jordan is intentionally restricting food intake (frequently skipping breakfast and lunch) while trying to lose weight quickly, and the fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance are consistent with under-fueling. He may ask the student for a detailed personalized eating plan.
referral_context.disclosure_guidance: Reveal information naturally based on the student's questions. Start with weakness/low energy during exercise. Only mention skipped meals if asked about energy, eating, recovery, or daily routine. Only reveal the rapid weight-loss goal with continued non-judgmental follow-up. If the student begins giving detailed advice, ask for an exact daily eating plan. Never say the full hidden concern immediately, never suggest a referral, and never name the type of professional who should help.

interprofessional_context.clinical_issue: Possible nutrition-related concern (intentional restrictive intake with rapid weight-loss goal) affecting energy and rehabilitation.
scope_considerations: General PT-related education about energy and activity may be appropriate.
Designing individualized diet plans or diagnosing an eating problem should not be assumed to be within the student's role.
safety_considerations: Urgency depends on what is disclosed (extent of restriction, rate of weight loss, other symptoms).

facts.text: His name is Jordan Mills, he is 24, and he goes by Jordan.
His knee pain is at the front of the knee, worse with squats, stairs, and longer gym sessions, and has built up over about two months.
He feels weak and unusually tired during some exercises lately, especially later in the day.
He trains at the gym five to six days a week and does not want to cut back.
He usually skips breakfast and often skips lunch too; most days his first real meal is in the evening.
He has been trying to lose weight quickly for the past couple of months and is deliberately eating much less; he is a bit defensive about it.
He would really like someone to just tell him exactly what to eat every day - he may push the student for a detailed personalized eating plan.
Sleep is okay, around 7 hours, though he sometimes wakes up hungry.
He works full-time at a logistics company and fits the gym around shifts.
He lives with a roommate; his gym friends are his main social circle.
His goals are to fix the knee, keep training hard, and 'get leaner'.
